lessons.title: Left-hand capitals (right Shift)
lessons.keys: Q W E R T A S D F G
lessons.tip: For a left-hand letter, hold the right Shift key with your right little finger. Hold Shift, type the letter, release.

tuto.intro: To write a capital letter, you hold down the Shift key, then type the letter. The golden rule: use the Shift key on the opposite hand to the letter. We start with the left-hand letters.

rules.d: Hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is NOT typing the letter: right Shift for a left-hand letter, left Shift for a right-hand letter. Both hands work together.
Press Shift and keep it down, type the letter, then let go of both. If you release Shift too early, you will get a lowercase letter.

rules.t: Words in capitals, and words with Q
rules.d: Here, several words are written entirely in capitals (WATER, GREAT): you hold Shift for the whole word. Words that start with Q (Queen, Quick) have just one capital, at the start.

tuto.tip: Goal: type left-hand capitals with the right Shift key, without hesitating.

lessons.text: Queen Quick Quiet Queue Quite Quake Quarter Question WATER GREAT STREET SWEET DESERT GRASS STARS WEST WEAR WASTE WET WE WAS EAST FAST FAT FED FAR FEW DAD DEAF DRAW FEAR GATE GAS GET GRADE STAGE DEGREE FREE

lessons.title: Right-hand capitals (left Shift)
lessons.keys: Y U I O P H J K L
lessons.tip: For a right-hand letter, hold the left Shift key with your left little finger. The same movement as before, on the other side.

tuto.intro: Same principle, on the other side: for a right-hand letter, you hold the left Shift key with your left little finger.

rules.d: Hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is NOT typing the letter: right Shift for a left-hand letter, left Shift for a right-hand letter. Both hands work together.
Press Shift and keep it down, type the letter, then let go of both. If you release Shift too early, you will get a lowercase letter.
Phil, Jill, Kylie, Kyle, Lily, Judy: names start with a capital letter. Words in capitals (HILL, POOL, YOU) make you hold Shift for longer.

tuto.tip: Goal: type right-hand capitals with the left Shift key, and alternate with the left hand.

lessons.text: Phil Jill Jack John Kylie Kyle Lily Judy Hope Jane JOLLY YOU JOY JOY HILL KILO YOLK POOL LOOK PUPIL YOU YOU HIP HIP HOP HOLY HI OIL PULL UP KILO KOI JUMP LUCK HOUR KIND

lessons.title: Bottom-row capitals
lessons.keys: Z X C V B N M
lessons.tip: For Z X C V B, hold right Shift. For N M, hold left Shift. The same rule: the hand opposite the letter.

tuto.intro: The bottom-row capitals are left. The rule does not change: Shift on the opposite hand. Z, X, C, V, B for the left hand; N and M for the right hand.

rules.d: Hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is NOT typing the letter: right Shift for a left-hand letter, left Shift for a right-hand letter. Both hands work together.
Press Shift and keep it down, type the letter, then let go of both. If you release Shift too early, you will get a lowercase letter.
With these seven letters, you know all 26 capitals. From here on, you can write proper names and the start of sentences.

tuto.tip: Goal: type the bottom-row capitals on both sides, choosing the right Shift key.

lessons.text: Zero Zoo Max Victor Nick Manchester Mark Molly ZOO ZERO ZOOM ZEBRA BOX MIX SIX FIX TAXI EXTRA VAN CAVE COVE COSY ZIP NOW MUM NINE CLUB BUS CAB VIVID EXAM CIVIC NOVEL CUB BAN SIX BOX NEXT NONE ZOO ZIP

lessons.title: Proper names and cities
lessons.tip: The names of people, cities and countries start with a capital letter. Keep your rhythm: Shift, letter, then the lowercase letters in one smooth run.

tuto.intro: Proper names, those of people, cities and countries, start with a capital letter. A chance to mix everything you have just learned.

rules.d: Oxford, York, Paris, Emma, Harry, Oscar: for each proper name, one Shift movement, then the lowercase letters in a flow.
Do not slow down after the capital: Shift and the letter form a single movement, and the lowercase letters follow.
Spot the next proper name before you reach it: your hand already knows which Shift key it will need.

tuto.tip: Goal: chain proper names together without breaking your rhythm.

lessons.text: Oxford, York, Derby, Paris, Liverpool, Manchester, Wales. Emma, Harry, Holly, Henry, Jane, Oscar, Lucy, Mark, Peter.

lessons.title: Correctly capitalised sentences
lessons.tip: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. After the full stop, a space, then the capital letter of the next sentence.

tuto.intro: A sentence always starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. You put it all into practice in real sentences.

rules.d: After the full stop, type a space, then the capital letter that opens the next sentence. This is a movement to make automatic.
Emma, Harry, Paris, Oxford: in the middle of a sentence, a proper name keeps its capital letter.
Before typing a word, ask yourself: start of a sentence? Proper name? If so, use the opposite Shift.

tuto.tip: Goal: type whole sentences with their capital letters, without hesitating over the Shift key.

lessons.text: Emma and Harry go to Oxford. They take a train with Oscar. It will be a good day in Oxford.
